    Construction

    Rim routed in two halves from 6/4 Honduran mahogany and glued on dowels, 2.25 in tall for a 2.5 in body: 7 mm walls, 12 × 8 mm glue ledges routed in place of kerfed linings, solid neck and tail blocks, open-top mortise for the set neck's tenon. The neck continues as a tongue under the fingerboard extension over the neck block, and its tenon drops through a notch in the top, so the neck goes on last. Every part is cut on a 3-axis router in one or two setups. Spruce top carved as flat planes: a 5 mm hexagonal bridge plateau inside a symmetric eight-sided arch zone, 14 facets in all, with a flat skirt outside it that lands on the rim. A 5 × 6 mm ring beam and two 6 × 9 mm parallel tone bars with scalloped ends run under the plateau's long sides, and a 6 × 7 mm cross bar braces the flat upper bout from the neck block. Top is quartersawn Sitka spruce, dyed black under the shellac, with a quarter-inch undyed band left around the edge as a faux binding. Back is quartersawn bigleaf maple with a single centre ridge 7 mm proud: two long flat panels meeting along the centreline, short pointed ends and a flat border, glued on and stiff enough to reflect energy back into the top without braces.

    No pickguard. An EMG 91 active floating humbucker hangs from a bracket under the fingerboard extension, and its lead drops into the body through a 6 mm hole hidden under the board. A stacked volume/tone pot with a concentric knob, a stereo output jack and a battery door share a 2 mm access plate on the flat treble lower-bout face of the rim. The 9 V slides end-first into a sleeve behind the door, so a battery change is a quarter-turn and no screws; the plate itself comes off only for wiring work, through the 84 × 30 mm window behind it. Being active, the EMG needs no string or tailpiece ground.
